title: Video courses for 300,000 students
summary: CursosMX sells recorded courses to 300,000 students in Mexico and Central America. Videos must arrive fast, raw recordings must cost little, and the login receives SQL injection attempts.

requirements.1: {{s1}} keeps copies of videos and images at points close to each student, so requests do not travel to the region every time.
requirements.2: {{s2}} is the origin of millions of videos that students watch every day over HTTP; the data stays in a single region in Mexico and there are no servers to manage.
requirements.3: {{s3}} keeps the raw recordings for 5 years, and they are almost never opened. What matters is the lowest cost per stored GB, even if reading them later costs more or takes longer.
requirements.4: {{s4}} holds the records for cursosmx.com and answers anyone on the internet who asks for that name, so they reach slot 1.
requirements.5: {{s5}} checks every HTTP request to the login and blocks SQL injection before it reaches the app.
requirements.6: The app load balancer spreads login and payments across the servers in the region.

s1.explanation: Cloud CDN uses the Google global edge network to serve content closer to users; it works with the global external Application Load Balancer. A dual-region bucket only replicates across two regions.

s2.explanation: Cloud Storage stores objects in buckets; a regional bucket in northamerica-south1 keeps the data in a single region in Mexico, and the Standard class is for frequently accessed data. A bucket can be the Cloud CDN origin.

s3.explanation: Archive is the lowest-cost Cloud Storage class, with a 365-day minimum and the highest access costs; data is readable in milliseconds, but every read is charged.
s3.hint_cue: the lowest cost per stored GB

s4.explanation: In Cloud DNS, a query from the internet is answered by the public zone. The private zone only answers VMs in authorized VPC networks.

s5.explanation: Cloud Armor attaches to the load balancer backend service and blocks requests before they reach the backends; its preconfigured WAF rules include signatures that detect SQL injection.

gcp-storage-dual-region.s1: A dual-region bucket replicates each object across a pair of regions, not at points close to each student.
gcp-storage-dual-region.s2: A dual-region bucket stores each object in a pair of regions, and Querétaro is not part of any pair; the requirement asks for a single region in Mexico.
gcp-storage-dual-region.s3: It uses the Standard class, meant for frequently accessed data; it is not the lowest-cost class per GB.

gcp-persistent-disk.s2: Persistent Disk adds block storage to a Compute Engine VM; it is not a bucket that serves videos over HTTP.
gcp-persistent-disk.s3: Persistent Disk is a VM disk, not a Cloud Storage class for keeping recordings for years at the lowest cost.

gcp-storage-nearline.s3: Nearline is low cost, but it is not the cheapest class; it has a 30-day minimum and is for infrequently accessed data.
gcp-storage-nearline.s2: Nearline charges to retrieve data and is for infrequent access; the videos are watched every day.

gcp-cloud-dns-private.s4: A private zone only answers VMs in authorized VPC networks; queries from the internet get the public zone.

gcp-vpc-firewall.s5: VPC firewall rules allow or deny connections by protocol, ports, source and destination; the SQL injection signatures live in the WAF rules of another service.
